Shared Grade 3 ancestry and weak local-rank proximity alone do not establish developmental direction, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. judgment.rationale: Both Skills are Grade 3 (rank 3, resolved coordinates) under READING AND PHONICS. The first is Term 2, Paired/Independent Reading: 'Reads aloud to a partner'; the second is Term 1, Group Guided Reading: 'Uses self-correcting strategies when reading: re-reading, pausing, practising a word before saying it aloud'. There is real, pair-specific instructional coherence: both concern accurate oral reading, and the self-correction bullet explicitly references rehearsing a word 'before saying it aloud', so the two reinforce one another as complementary oral-reading practices across adjacent terms and sub-strands. However, the Term 2 statement is an activity/participation format (reading aloud with a partner), not a deepening, broadening, or more complex version of self-monitoring and repair strategies; the bounded evidence gives no indication that proficiency in the Term 1 strategies is what raises the likelihood of success in the Term 2 partner read-aloud. The remaining nomination signals (shared Grade ancestor, rank gap 0 weak local-rank proximity, 'reading'/'fluency' LC tag overlap, 'a'/'aloud' token and trigram overlap) are shared-wording, hierarchy and LC overlap that cannot establish development. Symmetric relatesTo with canonical endpoint order and null direction is therefore the complete judgment. Material limits: both endpoints' source evidence (24 omitted items each) and LC evidence are truncated, and the Group Guided Reading vs Paired/Independent Reading sub-strands carry documented merge/audit context (distinct printed headings sharing table row 4), so the judgment rests on the quoted statement text and resolved Grade/Term scopes available here.

The second is a concurrent conceptual standard developing basic concepts of print (concept of book: cover, front, back, title; concept of text: word, letter, names of letters, one-to-one correspondence; directionality front-to-back and left-to-right, top-to-bottom; punctuation). Shared ancestors, LC tag/text token overlap and identical source page are proximity signals that cannot by themselves license direction. Symmetric relatesTo in canonical endpoint order with null direction is therefore the correct complete judgment. The pair-specific coherence is substantive rather than lexical: the self-monitoring/decoding repertoire and sustained independent text reading are complementary elements of the same term's reading programme, and the shared token overlap is minimal ('reading' only), so this is not a shared-wording or shared-hierarchy artefact. However, the evidence does not support a developmental dependency: both statements are prescribed simultaneously within the same Grade and the same Term under parallel sub-strands, the shared table row is documented upstream as a merged-cell layout region rather than ordering evidence, and the independent-reading statement is scoped to texts already familiar and at the child's own level, so proficiency in self-correction is not shown to be what enables it. A mirrored direction is equally arguable, so no buildsTowards direction is evidenced and the symmetric relatesTo is the correct judgment. Evidence limitation: 24 omitted source-evidence items per endpoint and truncated LC evidence for the first endpoint; judgment rests on the supplied statement texts, identity scopes, ancestors and LC tags.

judgment.rationale: First SFI: Grade 3 / Term 2 / Reading and Phonics / Shared Reading — 'Reads book as a whole class with the teacher (shared reading) and discusses the sequence of events, setting and cause-effect relations' (LCs: shared reading of a book; 'Discusses the sequence of events, setting and cause-effect relations in a book'). Second SFI: Grade 3 / Term 3 / Listening and Speaking (Oral) / Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities — 'Listens to a story and works out cause and effect in the story' (LCs: 'Listens to stories'; 'Works out cause and effect in the story'). Both resolve to Grade 3 (rank 3, status resolved), and Term 2 precedes Term 3, so a forward buildsTowards would be structurally permitted. Semantically, though, the pair shares a specific comprehension construct — identifying cause-and-effect relations in narrative — expressed in two complementary modalities (text-supported whole-class shared reading discussion versus oral comprehension of a heard story) and two different skill areas. The bounded evidence shows no substantive extension: no longer or harder text, no broader content, and no source-backed increase in independence (the Term 3 bullet sits under a teacher-led 'Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities' routine, and the Term 2 bullet already covers the richer set of sequence, setting and cause-effect). The overlap is therefore meaningful, pair-specific instructional coherence (same comprehension skill across reading and listening representations) rather than a developmental dependency, and it is clearly more than generic repeated wording. Canonical relatesTo with null direction is the correct judgment. judgment.rationale: First SFI is Grade 3 (rank 3, resolved), Term 4, Reading and Phonics / Phonics: 'Spells words correctly using their phonic knowledge in informal tests, in dictation and in all written work'. Second SFI is Grade 3 (rank 3, resolved), Term 3, Writing / Shared, Group and Independent Writing: 'Uses phonics knowledge and spelling rules to write unfamiliar words'. The two statements are substantively coherent in a pair-specific way: both require the learner to draw on phonic knowledge and spelling conventions to produce correctly spelled written words, one framed within composing/writing unfamiliar words and one within accurate spelling across dictation, informal tests and all written work. That is complementary cross-strand application and meaningful reinforcement, not merely shared vocabulary or shared Grade 3 ancestry. A within-grade buildsTowards from Term 3 to Term 4 is not justified: the first endpoint's supplied Learning Component metadata records the same 'spells words correctly ... in informal tests, in dictation and in all written work' skill under a Grade 3 Term 3 ancestor path (edf7e7dd / ab49385b / f54e6d5e / 216e4602), showing the Term 4 occurrence is CAPS repetition rather than an evidenced increase in demand, and no supplied text shows expanded scope, greater independence or added complexity in the first endpoint relative to the second. The opposite direction (Term 4 -> Term 3 within one Grade) is in any case invalid. relatesTo is therefore the correct symmetric judgment, with canonical endpoint order unchanged and null direction. judgment.rationale: Both are sibling bullets in the same Grade 3, Term 4, WRITING, 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' cell (page 132, same table row). 'Uses conjunctions to form compound sentences' is a sentence-level grammar skill; 'Uses apostrophes in contractions such as can't, Mary's' is a punctuation/orthography convention. They are complementary language-structure conventions applied in independent writing, mutually reinforcing written accuracy, but neither skill's proficiency is evidenced as supporting success in the other (joining clauses with conjunctions does not underpin apostrophe use, or vice versa), and they are at identical grade and term rank with no evidence of increased complexity in either direction. Shared parent, LC tag 'writing', and the trivially shared token 'uses' are not developmental evidence. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and ancestors carry merge/audit context, but the printed statement text is clear and sufficient for a symmetric coherence judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are Grade 2 (resolved rank 2) Skills in the Reading and Phonics Skill Area. The second SFI (Term 1, Sub-strand 'Group Guided Reading') is 'Reads both silently and aloud at own level in a Guided Reading group with teacher, that is, whole group reads same story based on the instructional reading level of the group'; the first SFI (Term 3, Sub-strand 'Paired/Independent Reading') is 'Reads aloud to a partner'. These are complementary daily reading arrangements rather than a developmental sequence: the first endpoint's source context labels state Paired/Independent reading is 'Daily reading related activities for 20 minutes while some groups are doing guided reading with the teacher', and the second endpoint's merge reason records a Paired/Independent Reading candidate inside the same Grade 2 Term 1 table, while the supplied LC metadata for 'reads aloud to a partner' lists several Grade 2 claims under different term ancestor paths. The Term 1 vs Term 3 offset therefore reflects the repeated CAPS table layout, not expanded capability; the later-term statement is in fact narrower (oral reading to a peer) than the earlier one (silent and aloud reading at instructional level), so no substantive extension, increased independence of the same capability, or deepening justifies buildsTowards in either direction. The nomination signals are lexical and hierarchical only (shared tokens 'reads'/'aloud', a shared Grade ancestor, rank gap 0 flagged 'weak'), which cannot establish dependency. There is nonetheless meaningful, pair-specific instructional coherence between teacher-scaffolded group oral reading and peer paired oral reading within the same Grade 2 Reading and Phonics programme, which exceeds generic repetition and supports symmetric relatesTo with canonical endpoint order preserved and null direction. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), the first endpoint's LC evidence is truncated, and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so certainty is moderate.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are Grade 2, Term 1, Reading and Phonics, Sub-strand 'Daily Phonic Activities of 15 minutes:' (Phonics), from the same source table row (page index 85). The second SFI is a word-level decoding element: revising common consonant digraphs (sh, ch, th) in word-final position with worked examples (fi-sh, ri-ch, clo-th). The first SFI requires applying words taught in phonics lessons in connected sentences and other texts. Secure recognition of the taught digraph patterns within words plausibly supports success in reading those phonics words in sentence- and text-level contexts, so the developmental direction runs from the element-level digraph revision to the applied text-level reading, not the reverse. Same Grade and same Term, so this direction is permitted (earlier/equal term). judgment.rationale: The first SFI (Grade 1, Term 4, Reading and Phonics / Daily Phonic Activities) is 'Groups common words into sound families', i.e. recognising shared spelling-sound patterns in high-frequency words. The second SFI (Grade 2, Term 3, Writing / Shared, Group and Independent Writing) is 'Spells common words correctly and attempts to spell unfamiliar words using phonic knowledge', decomposed into LCs 'Spells common words correctly' and 'Attempts to spell unfamiliar words using phonic knowledge'. This is not mere repeated wording: the Grade 1 skill is receptive/analytic grouping of word families in phonics, while the Grade 2 skill applies that phonic word-family knowledge productively in independent writing, extending to unfamiliar words. Proficiency in grouping words into sound families plausibly supports accurate spelling and phonic decoding-for-encoding of new words. Canonical coordinates are resolved Grade 1 (rank 1) to Grade 2 (rank 2), so the lower-to-higher first_to_second direction is permitted and appropriate. Both endpoints' source evidence excerpts are truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and all nodes carry upstream audit/merge context, but the statement texts, Skill Area and Sub-strand placements are intact and sufficient for this judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints sit at Grade 1 (rank 1). The second SFI is Grade 1 / Term 1 / Reading and Phonics / Emergent reading skills: 'Develops basic concepts of print including ... Punctuation: capital letter, lowercase letter, full stop, comma, question mark' (LC 'Develops the concept of punctuation: capital letter, lowercase letter, full stop, comma, question mark'), establishing the print concepts and names of these marks in reading. The first SFI is Grade 1 / Term 4 / Listening and Speaking: 'Uses terms such as sentence, capital letter, full stop', which requires the learner to actively use that metalanguage orally. Knowing and recognising the punctuation/print concepts in Term 1 plausibly supports confident oral use of the same terminology in Term 4, so the permitted direction is the earlier Term 1 item to the later Term 4 item (second_to_first); the reverse within-grade direction would be invalid. Overlap is not merely lexical: the shared 'capital letter / full stop' terminology is the substantive content of both statements, applied first as print-concept recognition and then as expressive use of terms across a different skill area. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and both carry upstream audit/merge context, so confidence is moderate.
